questions.prompt: A business sells things to…
questions.explanation: Businesses sell goods or services to customers.

questions.prompt: The money a business keeps after paying for everything is called…
questions.explanation: Profit = money in − money out.

questions.prompt: You sell lemonade for ${s} and spent ${c} on lemons. What is your profit?
questions.explanation: ${s} − ${c} = ${ANSWER} profit.

questions.prompt: Things a business must pay for, like supplies and rent, are called…
questions.explanation: Costs are the money a business spends.

questions.prompt: You sell {n} cookies for ${p} each. How much money comes in (revenue)?
questions.explanation: {n} × ${p} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: If costs are bigger than sales, the business loses money.
questions.explanation: True! That's called a loss.

questions.prompt: Revenue ${r}, costs ${c}. Profit?
questions.explanation: ${r} − ${c} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: It's raining at the night market. What usually happens?
questions.explanation: Bad weather keeps people home, so a smart seller makes fewer snacks.

questions.prompt: You made 100 dumplings but only sold 60. What happens to the other 40?
choices: They’re wasted, and you paid for them
They turn into money at midnight
Customers have to pay for them anyway
questions.explanation: Making too many wastes money on supplies.

questions.prompt: Another stall sells the same snack for less. To keep customers you could…
choices: Make yours tastier or cut the price a bit
Raise your price a lot so it looks fancy
Ask the other stall to close down
questions.explanation: Competition pushes businesses to be better or cheaper.

questions.prompt: Each dumpling costs $1 to make and sells for $3. Profit for {n} dumplings?
If you raise your price a LOT, what might happen?
questions.explanation: Higher prices usually mean fewer buyers.

questions.prompt: Someone who starts their own business is called an…
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs start and run businesses.

questions.prompt: Stall rent is $10 a night. You sell $50 of snacks that cost $15 to make. Profit for the night?
Why might a business buy a fancy sign?
choices: To make the stall lose money
questions.explanation: Spending money to earn more money later is called investing in your business.

questions.prompt: Supplies cost $12. Each cup sells for $2. How many cups to get back the $12?
questions.explanation: $12 ÷ $2 = 6 cups. That's the break-even point!

questions.prompt: Big ships in the harbor carry…
choices: Tourists who want a free ride
questions.explanation: Ships carry goods around the world. That's trade!

questions.prompt: Buying things from another country is called…
questions.explanation: Import = bring in. Export = send out.

questions.prompt: Selling things to another country is called…
questions.explanation: Exporting sends goods out to other countries.

questions.prompt: Buy low, sell high means…
choices: Buy cheap, then sell for more
Buy things from a high shelf
questions.explanation: Traders earn money from price differences.

questions.prompt: You buy tea for ${b} in Hong Kong and sell it for ${s} in London. Profit per box?
questions.explanation: ${s} − ${b} = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: If you bring LOTS of tea to one town, the price of tea there will probably…
questions.explanation: When there's a lot of something, sellers lower prices to sell it.

questions.prompt: Shipping goods across the ocean costs money. A trader should…
choices: Make sure profit beats shipping costs
Ignore shipping costs, they are small
Send the boats out empty to save money
questions.explanation: Profit must cover all costs, including shipping.

questions.prompt: You buy 10 boxes for $5 each and sell them for $8 each. Shipping costs $10. Total profit?
questions.explanation: Sales $80 − cost $50 − shipping $10 = $20.

questions.prompt: Delivery riders often get a little extra money from happy customers. That's called a…
questions.explanation: Tips are extra money for good service.

questions.prompt: You earn $5 per delivery plus a ${t} tip. How much for one delivery?
Why might delivering food FAST earn more?
choices: People tip more for hot, fast food
Driving fast costs nothing at all
Nobody cares how long food takes
questions.explanation: Great service often earns bigger tips.

questions.prompt: Writing down all the money in and out of a business is called…
questions.explanation: Bookkeeping keeps track of the money.

questions.prompt: Receipts: $4, $7, $3, $6. Total?
A business owner's notebook says $50 came in, but the cash box has $45. What should they do?
choices: Check each sale to find the mistake
Ask the next customer for $5 more
questions.explanation: Finding mistakes keeps the books accurate.

questions.prompt: A good business plan answers…
choices: What you sell, who buys it, costs and prices
Your favorite color and favorite snack
Nothing important, just the opening day
Only the name of the business
questions.explanation: A plan helps you know if you can make a profit.

questions.prompt: Which is a business?
questions.explanation: A bakery sells goods to customers.

questions.prompt: A haircut is a service. Bread is a…
questions.explanation: Goods are things; services are actions people do for you.

questions.prompt: Hiring a helper at your stall costs money. It's a good idea when…
choices: They help you sell more than they cost
Never, helpers always cost too much
Always, no matter what they cost
Only on Sundays when it is quiet
questions.explanation: Helpers are worth it if they bring in more than they cost.

questions.prompt: Your helper costs $20 a day and helps you sell $35 more. How much better off are you?
During a festival, crowds are huge. A smart stall owner…
questions.explanation: More customers means more demand, be ready!

questions.prompt: Profit ÷ sales tells you…
choices: How much of each dollar you keep
How many customers you have today
What the weather will be tomorrow
How old your business is in years
questions.explanation: That's the profit margin, the share of sales you keep.

questions.prompt: Your business made $30 profit. A smart plan is to…
choices: Save some to grow the business
Spend all of it right away
Give it all to the stall next door
questions.explanation: Saving profits helps your business grow.

questions.prompt: Every business makes money from day one.
questions.explanation: False! Many businesses lose money at first while they grow.

questions.prompt: Hong Kong has a busy harbor because…
choices: Lots of ships come to trade
Ships are afraid of other ports
questions.explanation: Hong Kong is a famous trading city.

questions.prompt: Bubble tea costs $2 to make. You sell it for $4. Profit per cup?
Which is a COST for a lemonade stand?
questions.explanation: Things you must buy to make lemonade are costs.

questions.prompt: Your stall ran out of food early and customers left sad. Next time you should…
questions.explanation: Running out loses sales and makes customers unhappy.

questions.prompt: Electronics are cheap where they're made and expensive far away. Why?
choices: Shipping them far away costs money
They are made with magic up close
They get heavier the farther they go
They are not really more expensive
questions.explanation: Shipping costs and scarcity raise prices far away.

questions.prompt: Rent $100/month. You earn $4 profit per cake (before rent). How many cakes to pay the rent?
Customers love your dumplings and tell friends. That's good…
questions.explanation: A good reputation brings more customers.

questions.prompt: When something is hard to find but everybody wants it, its price…
questions.explanation: High demand + low supply = higher price.

questions.prompt: You sold 8 kites at $6. Kite supplies cost $2 each. Profit?
questions.explanation: Revenue 8 × $6 = $48. Costs 8 × $2 = $16. Profit $32.

questions.prompt: Which is the BEST reason to start a business?
choices: It solves a problem people pay for
You want to be on TV someday
Your friend told you to do it
questions.explanation: Successful businesses solve real problems for customers.

questions.prompt: Gas for the delivery scooter costs money. A shorter route means…
choices: More gas used on every trip
questions.explanation: Planning short routes saves money on fuel.

questions.prompt: Revenue and profit mean the same thing.
questions.explanation: False! Revenue is all the money in. Profit is what's left after costs.

questions.prompt: Morning sales $18, evening sales $27. Total revenue?
